title: DOJ's March 2025 Epstein Review Emails: Public-Figure Flags, Victim Protections and the Missing Plan
summary: A DOJ FOIA release dated October 9, 2026 documents March 2025 public-figure review flags and victim-redaction guidance. The operative plan remains partly withheld; a separate October 9 court order sets an October 16 in-camera deadline.
evidence_boundary: March 2025 review instructions and flagged names are not proof of withholding.

title: FBI Vault Part 13: March Redaction Orders, July Statement Emails, and the Phang Case
summary: FBI Vault Part 13 documents March 22, 2025 redaction guidance and July 3 FBI–DOJ statement coordination. A source audit distinguishes that record from the later Phang v. Blanche administrative-record dispute.
evidence_boundary: 2025 FBI redaction records must not be conflated with later court proceedings.

title: Wyden’s Missing Banker 302 vs. Three Public Deutsche Interviews
summary: DOJ released three Deutsche-linked FBI FD-302 interviews. Wyden says another banker interview report remains unreleased. GAH cross-checks the public 302s, a planned Paul Morris proffer, and the open receipt gap.
evidence_boundary: Three public Deutsche Bank-linked FD-302s do not identify Wyden's unnamed missing banker.

title: Nine SARs, $1.28 Billion, and the Reporting Gap in Epstein’s JPMorgan Accounts
summary: A source-bound reconstruction of nine JPMorgan suspicious-activity reports involving Jeffrey Epstein: seven reports before 2019 totaling $4.3 million, then two 2019 reports covering about $1.283 billion.
evidence_boundary: Suspicious-activity reports are transaction reporting, not findings of criminal guilt.

title: December 6–7, 2007: The Victim Letters, the Defense Papers, and the Missing Decision Record
summary: A source-bound reconstruction of the 48 hours before Jeffrey Epstein victim-notification letters were halted: an FBI warning, defense filings, a native two-minute email sequence, and the unresolved identity behind the final hold.
evidence_boundary: The public record does not establish the decision maker behind the victim-letter hold.

title: Why the Chinese Consortium Declined the GADECO Deal: Missing Accounts and a $1.6 Billion Valuation
summary: Original 2014 correspondence and engineering records show why Joachim Chao's consortium declined a proposed GADECO deal: disputed historical financials, a $1.6B asking price, and projections dependent on future oil production.
evidence_boundary: A proposed $1.6B acquisition and contingent fees are not a verified sale or payment.

title: A Proposed $200 Million Saudi–Israeli Healthcare Fund, Documented but Not Funded
summary: 2015 correspondence describes Saudi investor recruitment, a proposed Luxembourg healthcare fund naming Ehud Barak, and preliminary Rothschild discussions. No funding or launch is proven.
evidence_boundary: A 2015 proposed fund is not evidence that the vehicle was financed or launched.

title: Barak's 2015 Putin Meeting Request: An Official Refusal, Not a Completed Appointment
summary: A Russian presidential aide's office declined a June 2015 appointment request from Ehud Barak. Separate claims of an earlier Putin meeting require independent corroboration.
evidence_boundary: A documented refused appointment is not proof of an earlier or completed meeting.

title: Fourteen Barak Archive Leads: Verified Documents, Corrections and Open Receipts
summary: The Barak archive evidence ledger reconciles 14 leads, clarifies the GADECO timeline and the Rialm-NYC deed, and preserves uncertainty about meetings and payments.
evidence_boundary: Leads and records carry different proof levels; the index distinguishes proposed from completed.

title: Børge Brende & Epstein: Norway’s 2017 Email Question
summary: A source-first reconstruction of Børge Brende’s September 30, 2026 parliamentary testimony: his stated 2018 first meeting with Jeffrey Epstein, the unresolved 2017 “Norwegian friend” email, the 2018 WEF/UN exchange, and the limits of the record.
evidence_boundary: 2017 references and the claimed first meeting require separate corroboration.

title: George Mitchell in the Epstein Records: What Resolves Cleanly—and What Does Not
summary: A source audit separating George Mitchell from namesake collisions, sworn allegations, denials, post-2008 contact records, and unresolved attribution questions in the Epstein archive.
evidence_boundary: Namesakes, allegations, denials and independent contact records are separate evidence classes.

title: The Andriesz Paper Trail: FBI Hits, CFTC, HMRC and FCA Review
summary: A source-controlled audit of the Simon Andriesz record across the FBI, CFTC, HMRC, FCA, the UK Employment Tribunal and the AdFin corporate file—separating confirmed regulator actions from allegations and unresolved causation.
evidence_boundary: Separate regulator proceedings cannot be merged into a single causal finding.

title: New DOJ Release Documents March 2025 Epstein File Review Instructions
summary: A 41-page DOJ disclosure identifies instructions to flag public figures and protect victim identities. The approved review plan remains partly withheld.
evidence_boundary: Flagging public figures for review is not proof of hiding records.

title: Judge Orders Redacted FBI Notes for Private Review by October 16
summary: A signed October 9 order requires three sets of handwritten FBI notes to be submitted to the judge. It does not require public release.
evidence_boundary: October 16 in-camera deadline is not an order to publish the notes that day.

title: Why a Chinese Consortium Declined a Proposed $1.6 Billion Oil Deal
summary: November 2014 correspondence and engineering forecasts explain the dispute over financial disclosure and price. A completed sale has not been established.
evidence_boundary: The offer and broker fee proposals have no established closing or payment.
